title: Licences in practice: AGPL, GPL, MIT, OpenRAIL
hook: Most of the time nothing is triggered until you hand over a copy or put it on a website. Read what four real licences ask in five ordinary cases. Not legal advice.

verified.claim: GPL-3.0 section 0: mere interaction over a network with no transfer of a copy is not conveying.
AGPL-3.0 section 13: a modified version must prominently offer remote users its Corresponding Source.
GPL-3.0 section 5: modified source versions need notices of the change and stay under the licence.
MIT's condition is keeping the copyright and permission notice in all copies or substantial portions.
Apache-2.0 4(b) asks modified files to carry notices that you changed them.
CreativeML Open RAIL-M paragraphs 4 and 5 and Attachment A set use restrictions, which pass down, also for hosting.
verified.ref: license.txt from the CompVis Space, fetched 2026-11-01

verified.claim: Software with no licence generally gives you no permission to use, modify or share it.
ComfyUI's own LICENSE is GPL version 3.

unchecked: This is a reader's summary and not legal advice. Courts, jurisdictions and specific facts can change the answer. Ask someone qualified if it matters.
What counts as a derivative or a covered work, including whether a node pack is one with ComfyUI, is a real legal question that we don't answer here.
Other RAIL variants and model licences differ. We read only this one.
The table simplifies. It doesn't cover patents, warranty terms or every condition.
